Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
Data Scientist | Applied Machine Learning

Edinburgh, UK | tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | +44 7700 900110 | linkedin.com/in/tmh-example

PROFILE
Data scientist with 6 years of experience in analytics and data science, including more than 4 years in data science roles. Builds and evaluates forecasting and customer-propensity models, develops feature-engineered workflows in Python and SQL, and translates business needs into practical analytical tools. Experience includes scheduled model scoring and forecasting workflows using BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, a Dockerized Streamlit experiment tool, and automated tests for forecasting feature code. Seeking to develop further in machine learning engineering and production systems.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python (pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels, pytest), SQL (BigQuery), dbt, Git, Docker, Streamlit, R (tidyverse, brms), Vertex AI Workbench, Looker, Jupyter
Machine learning: Feature engineering, forecasting, churn propensity modelling, model evaluation, SHAP
Statistics: A/B testing, sequential testing, causal inference, Bayesian statistics, time-series forecasting

EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox (meal-kit subscriptions), Edinburgh
Feb 2022–Present
- Built a weekly, six-week-ahead demand forecasting workflow by recipe and region using LightGBM and calendar, price and menu-position features. The scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook writes forecasts to BigQuery for operations reporting in Looker; WAPE fell from 23% to 14%, with estimated food waste reduction of 9%.
- Developed an XGBoost churn propensity model scored weekly in BigQuery, with retention offers targeted to top-decile customers. A 10% holdout validated a 2.1 percentage-point reduction in churn in the treated group.
- Design and analyse approximately 40 A/B tests each year for growth and product teams; built a sequential testing calculator used by around 25 colleagues, writing the Python Streamlit app and its Dockerfile. The data platform team manages its Cloud Run deployment.
- Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer.
- Since 2025, have written pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage.
- Present results to leadership monthly and delivered the internal “Stats for PMs” training three times.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail, Glasgow
Sep 2020–Jan 2022
- Performed customer segmentation and tariff analysis using R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team about two days each month.

SELECTED PROJECT
Image Classification Course Project | Personal, 2025
- Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food-images dataset as part of an online deep learning course; achieved approximately 80% accuracy. Learning project.
- Tools: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab.

EDUCATION
MSc Statistics, University of the Lothians | 2020 | Distinction
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models for small-area energy demand

BSc Mathematics, University of the Lothians | 2019

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Swahili (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, clear and professional CV with a logical structure, reverse-chronological experience, relevant technical skills, and quantified outcomes. The Thistlebox bullets are particularly effective: they explain the modelling approach, workflow, business use and measurable impact. The CV is also commendably transparent about the scope of the candidate's production experience, such as scheduled notebooks, batch scoring and platform-managed deployment. The main content limitation is not poor writing but the candidate's current profile: this is a Data Scientist moving toward Machine Learning Engineering, rather than an established MLE with end-to-end ownership of production AI systems.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly parseable: it uses standard headings, plain text, conventional dates, readable bullets and no problematic tables, graphics or multi-column formatting. Relevant ATS terms such as Python, SQL, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Docker, Streamlit, pytest, feature engineering, model evaluation, forecasting, scheduled workflows and batch scoring are present. For this specific vacancy, AI screening probability is moderate to low because several mandatory terms are either absent or unsupported by the candidate's background: RAG, chat assistants, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, and named MLOps tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow or Airflow. These gaps should not be filled with unsupported keywords. The CV could, however, make the supported production engineering and cloud experience easier for an ATS to identify by grouping it more explicitly.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's Python, GCP, feature engineering, model evaluation, scheduled ML workflow and automated testing aspects. It also demonstrates practical ownership, communication with product and growth teams, operational impact, and a pragmatic focus on tools used by colleagues and operations. The candidate's forecasting workflow, churn batch scoring and Streamlit/Docker tool are relevant examples of applied ML systems. However, the candidate's material shows gaps against several must-have requirements: there is no four-year history as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production; no chat assistant or RAG experience; no personally owned model serving/API deployment; no demonstrated monitoring or data versioning; no named MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or equivalent MLOps platform; and no clearly documented data ingestion pipeline experience. The degrees are Statistics and Mathematics rather than machine learning, computer science or an engineering degree. These are genuine qualification gaps rather than CV-writing defects. The CV nevertheless presents a credible adjacent profile for a junior or transitional MLE position.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS/alignment enhancements:
1. In the Technical Skills section, reorganize the current single-line skills list into clearly labelled lines without adding unsupported tools: "Languages & ML: Python (pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels, pytest); SQL (BigQuery); R (tidyverse, brms)"; "Cloud & data platforms: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, Looker"; "Engineering & applications: Git, Docker, Streamlit, Jupyter"; "ML methods: Feature engineering, forecasting, churn propensity modelling, model evaluation, SHAP"; and "Statistics: A/B testing, sequential testing, causal inference, Bayesian statistics, time-series forecasting." This makes the supported cloud, engineering, testing and feature-engineering terms easier for ATS screening to parse.
2. In the Professional Profile, replace the final sentence, "Seeking to develop further in machine learning engineering and production systems," with a more evidence-led statement such as: "Experienced in scheduled batch ML workflows, BigQuery scoring, Dockerized analytical tools and automated testing; now moving toward broader machine learning engineering and production systems." This preserves the truthful career direction while foregrounding the production-related experience already demonstrated elsewhere in the CV.
3. In the Thistlebox forecasting bullet, explicitly use the supported term "feature engineering" by changing "using LightGBM and calendar, price and menu-position features" to "using LightGBM and feature engineering based on calendar, price and menu-position variables." Do not add claims about model serving, monitoring or data versioning.
4. In the Thistlebox churn bullet, make the deployment mode unambiguous for both recruiters and ATS systems by changing "Developed an XGBoost churn propensity model scored weekly in BigQuery" to "Developed an XGBoost churn propensity model with weekly batch scoring in BigQuery." This accurately distinguishes the work from API-based model serving.
5. In the Thistlebox SQL/dbt bullet, change "Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer" to "Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models supporting the analytics data-transformation layer." This gives the existing data-pipeline-related work clearer wording without claiming unsupported data ingestion ownership.

Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)
